title: Staged traffic taper and verifiable backup assertion playbook for active-passive DR drills
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Goal: Define and validate an operational playbook to (1) perform an active->passive regional failover rehearsal with a staged traffic taper (traffic tapering rather than abrupt cutover), (2) verify backup integrity and restore correctness with cryptographic checksums and query-level reconciliation, and (3) exercise circuit-breaker and load-shedding thresholds to ensure graceful degradation within SLOs. This ticket covers runbook creation, test harness automation, and a scheduled drill with clear success criteria and rollback plans.

Scope: Redwood serving runtime + tokenstore + routing layer + console dashboards. Drill will be executed in a canary fashion (one customer segment, then internal services) in the eu-west and us-east pairs. Non-goals: This ticket does not change production SLOs; it codifies validation and operations steps.

Why now: Recent table-top identified gaps in staged tapering, and SLI scatterplots show latency spikes when traffic is abruptly moved. A softer taper + backup checksum validation reduced previous incidents in experiments. We need an operable playbook and automated assertions to reduce manual verification time during drills.
steps: Pre-drill: roster & approvals: get SRE, runtime, routing, on-call, and console owners. Post calendar invite with runbook and Slack channel #dr-drills.
1) Baseline capture (T -72h to T -1h): capture 1h p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token/sec, queue depth, GPU util per node. Persist to a drill bucket and tag dashboards.
2) Snapshot & checksum (T -48h): take application-consistent snapshots of tokenstore and model cache manifests. Generate SHA256 checksums for each snapshot and store in vault (kms-wrapped).

3) Backup smoke restores (T -36h): run automated small-restores into isolated staging cluster and run integrity queries. Assert row counts and hash prefixes match production. Failure -> abort drill and open INC ticket.

4) Canary traffic taper (T -10m): route 5% of traffic to passive region using routing policy 'taper/5pct'. Monitor SLOs for 15m. If error-rate or latency SLOs breach, increase circuit breaker sensitivity and revert taper (see rollback).

5) Progressive taper steps: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over N minutes with verification gates at each step. Gates: no p99 spike > 2x baseline AND error rate < 0.5% absolute increase OR error budget remaining > 60%.

6) Load-shedding triggers: if queue depth > 5000 or GPU util > 90% sustained for 120s, begin per-route shedding order (lowest priority customers first) and enable graceful rejection (429 + retry-after). Document affected routes.
7) Circuit breaker exercise: intentionally trip one routing plane circuit breaker to validate automated fallback to smaller model variant and verify end-to-end response semantics and telemetry.

8) Full passive activation (if all gates pass): declare passive region 'active-for-drill' and run synthetic end-to-end test suite (API generation and embedding flows) against the passive region. Verify feature parity and KV cache warmup.

9) Restore verification: run deterministic queries against restored data and compare SHA256 fingerprints of key prefixes and a randomized 1k-record sample for content equality. Run diff tool and produce an integrity report.
10) Reconciliation and rollback (post-drill): roll traffic back in staged steps, re-run smoke restores in primary to validate write-path. Summarize learnings and open follow-ups for discrepancies.
Post-drill: 2 hour debrief, 48h action items, and 7-day follow-up on any rolling fixes.
validation_criteria: SLOs must hold for the canary segment: availability >= 99.95% and p99 latency <= 1200ms during the canary window.
Backup checksum parity: all snapshot checksums in vault match checksums computed from the restore target.
Restore correctness: randomized sample compare must show 0 mismatches in primary key fields for the 1k sample. Any mismatch triggers an incident and test re-run.
Circuit-breaker fallback must preserve response schema and return canonical error codes. No silent data corruption allowed.
Automated runbook assertions (scripts) must complete within 10 minutes at each gate or mark the gate failed.

metrics_and_alerts: Primary SLI: availability measured as 5xx+timeouts rate per minute
Latency SLIs: p50/p95/p99 by route. Alert on p99 > baseline*1.8 for 10m
Error budget burn alert: configured at 40% remaining -> paging SRE
Queue-depth alert: queue_depth > 5000 -> trigger load-shed orchestration
GPU util alert: per-node GPU_util > 90% for 120s -> auto-shed lowest priority routes
rollback_plan: Immediate stop: Use routing plane to revert taper to original percentage within 1 minute.
Failback: if passive region shows state divergence (>0 mismatches) or SLOs breached persistently, run orchestrated failback to primary and restore from pre-drill snapshots.
Mitigations: enable safe-mode routing (reject heavy generation workloads, route to smaller model) and disable automatic autoscaling to avoid burst churn.
Communication: page on-call, update #dr-drills with status, and send a one-line to customers if customer-impact = high.
